text:
alex: hey @eng-infra — we're onboarding a new enterprise customer who needs low-latency GPU inference in us-west-2. Planning 4 p4d nodes initially (burst to 12). Need guidance on VPC layout, TGW peering from customer account to our hub, and quota increases (EIP, p4d, ENI). Who can help with the AWS quota requests and subnet sizing?

tara: which account and CIDR plan? are they using host-network for pods or CNI IP allocation? need to know to size subnets.

alex: customer acct 987654321000, hub acct 123456789012. We'll run k8s on the GPU instances with AWS CNI (default) for now. Want per-az GPU subnets and a central hub NAT in our infra account. Initial requirement: 4 p4d spread across 2 AZs, target eventual 12 across 3 AZs.

mike: fyi p4d instances consume multiple ENIs/addresses per instance depending on instance type and eni limits for ENI per instance. Also watch ENI quota per region for the account that will attach to TGW.

leila: for subnet sizing I recommend reserving /22 for the GPU subnets per AZ (1022 usable) if you expect many pods or sidecars; /24 will be tight if you scale to many replicas. Also consider enabling prefix delegation on CNI to avoid running out of IPs.

sam: I'll open quota requests. We should ask AWS to increase: EC2 On-Demand limit for p4d.24xlarge to 8 in us-west-2, Elastic IP quota in hub to 200, VPC ENI quota to 5000, and NAT Gateway limit to 50. Any other quotas to mention?

mika: PrivateLink note — the customer wants access to our model-registry API without internet exposure. We'll need an Interface Endpoint in customer VPC that connects to our endpoint service in the hub. That requires an NLB in the hub and acceptance settings. Cross-account endpoint service needs allowed principals or acceptance workflows.

alex: thanks. For the hub NAT: cost-wise NAT Gateway per AZ is expensive (hourly + per-GB). Is it worth centralizing NAT in the hub via TGW route to reduce EIP count and control egress? Pros/cons?

leila: central NAT in hub is fine; but be mindful of SNAT port exhaustion if lots of concurrent outbound connections from many pods. For high-conn workloads consider Egress NAT instances with autoscaling or use AWS NAT Gateway with EIP pool scaling. Also check route table size for TGW attachments.

mike: also check ephemeral port behavior — if inference clients open many outbound connections (e.g., to metrics or 3rd-party APIs), you may hit SNAT limits. If we centralize, we need more EIPs or use Elastic Network Interfaces in EC2 NAT instances and source NAT aggregation.

sam: opened AWS case #1234567890: request increases mentioned above. ETA from support ~24-72h for initial review. I added justification: production inference, low-latency SLA, cross-account TGW attachments.

infra-bot: AWS case #1234567890 created by sam. Status: awaiting AWS response.

alex: subnet terraform snippet suggestion?

tara: paste below — simple example, adjust names/azs:

```hcl
resource "aws_vpc" "gpu_vpc" {
  cidr_block = "10.40.0.0/20"
  tags = { Name = "gpu-vpc" }
}
resource "aws_subnet" "gpu_az1" {
  vpc_id = aws_vpc.gpu_vpc.id
  cidr_block = "10.40.0.0/22"
  availability_zone = "us-west-2a"
}
```

leila: remember to set NAT routing in hub route table to point TGW -> hub NAT attachment and configure TGW route propagation. Also add security group for PrivateLink NLB to allow customer VPC CIDRs.

sam: once AWS approves quotas I'll request the customer account create the TGW attachment and we accept. Plan: provision NLB + endpoint service in hub, share allowed principals (customer acct id), create interface endpoints on customer side, then configure TGW routes and route tables.

alex: perfect. timeline: target infra ready in 1 week after quota approval. Thanks all :rocket:
